CALL.meaning: Incoming remote call recorded by the receiving component; its elapsed interval includes work delegated to other components.
CALL.read: Use Context and Func to locate BSL, and CallID with client identities to find the caller. duration and CpuTime are microseconds; Memory/MemoryPeak and disk InBytes/OutBytes are bytes. Nested SDBL/DB events can explain part of this interval.
CALL.badSigns: A call exceeds the operation's measured budget, repeats per processed row, or has a MemoryPeak that grows with the result set.
CALL.traps: One CALL is not necessarily one user action. Summing nested calls or adding their DB durations double counts elapsed work.
CALL.fixes: Use the scenario profile to separate SQL, waits and exchanges; batch repeated server work and reduce form data when that component dominates.
CALL.cost: Unfiltered CALL records scale with remote-call frequency; Context adds stack text to each record.

thresholds.text: Standard 487 recommends no additional client-code server calls for a typical user action unless justified; it supplies no universal millisecond CALL limit. Assess elapsed time against the measured operation budget.

SCALL.meaning: Outgoing remote call recorded by the component making the call.
SCALL.read: Match CallID, ClientID/DstClientID and IName/MName to a receiving CALL within compatible intervals. duration is microseconds; inspect the receiver's nested work before attributing the delay.
SCALL.badSigns: Repeated calls to the same MName during one action, or a long SCALL whose receiver also runs slowly.
SCALL.traps: Starkov's pairing method needs both sides. [unverified] Subtracting CALL from SCALL does not isolate pure network time without validating the pair and its boundaries.
SCALL.fixes: Combine per-row requests into one server call; investigate the receiving CALL and measure exchange time separately.
SCALL.cost: Busy clients can emit many short SCALL records; duration filtering hides call-count problems.

SDBL.meaning: Operation against the platform data model, including queries and transaction actions.
SDBL.read: Read Func, Sdbl, Context and t:connectID. BeginTransaction, CommitTransaction and RollbackTransaction delimit transactions; inspect nested DB events for the physical SQL. Record duration is microseconds.
SDBL.badSigns: Repeated Sdbl text in a loop, or long transaction intervals with TLOCK waiters; large SDBL intervals unexplained by captured DB work need further profiling.
SDBL.traps: HoldConnection and transaction markers are not SQL statements. Adding SDBL duration to nested DB duration counts the same work twice.
SDBL.fixes: Replace repeated model queries with a batch; move permissible computation outside transactions and inspect the corresponding DB plan.
SDBL.cost: SDBL includes frequent data-model operations and transaction markers; all-properties capture can produce large volumes.
SDBL.exampleNote: [illustrative] A transaction-begin marker with no previously active transaction. All names and values are synthetic.

DBMSSQL.meaning: Execution of a SQL statement by Microsoft SQL Server on behalf of 1C.
DBMSSQL.read: Read Sql and parameters with Context; dbpid identifies the DBMS connection. Compare duration in microseconds, returned Rows and RowsAffected. Optional planSQLText explains access; lka/lkp annotate observed blocking.
DBMSSQL.badSigns: A SQL fingerprint dominates cumulative elapsed time, or a slow statement has confirmed blocking or excessive reads in its plan.
DBMSSQL.traps: Published Infostart examples contain RowsAffected=-1; do not interpret it as negative updates. Physical SQL table names require the investigated infobase's database structure; duration alone does not separate CPU, I/O and waits.
DBMSSQL.fixes: Find the BSL query, inspect actual data, statistics, plan and waits, then adjust predicates, indexes or transaction scope and re-measure.
DBMSSQL.cost: SQL text and parameters make frequent DBMSSQL records large; plans and DBMS lock polling add instrumentation cost even when output is filtered.

thresholds.text: Gilev team's historical slow-query monitoring setup defaults to 10 s; lower cutoffs increase collection load. This is a monitoring choice, not a universal SQL health boundary.

DBPOSTGRS.meaning: Execution of SQL by PostgreSQL on behalf of the platform.
DBPOSTGRS.read: Use Sql, Context and dbpid to locate the BSL operation and DBMS connection. duration is microseconds. With optional planSQLText, compare estimated and actual rows and account for loops; actual time is milliseconds.
DBPOSTGRS.badSigns: Repeated SQL dominates the operation, actual row counts diverge from estimates, or a measured plan spends most time scanning or joining excess data.
DBPOSTGRS.traps: PostgreSQL cost is an estimate in planner units, not seconds. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes SQL; platform connection settings affect reproducibility.
DBPOSTGRS.fixes: Check waits and statistics, push selective restrictions into the 1C query, and validate suitable indexes against the measured plan on comparable data.
DBPOSTGRS.cost: DBPOSTGRS can dominate log volume. IBS's five-second example still produced hundreds of MB; use plans on test/development per the official methodology.

thresholds.text: Evgeny Filippov / IBS uses durationus >= 5000000 (5 s) in a concrete PostgreSQL capture. This is an author-specific collection cutoff, not proof that shorter queries are normal.

Gilev team's older monitoring example for SQL Server/PostgreSQL instead defaults to 10 s. Its cutoff differs from the IBS 5 s capture above; both are collection policies, not competing universal health limits.
The official PostgreSQL methodology uses about 50% DBPOSTGRS/CALL elapsed share as a reason to investigate SQL. Compare non-overlapping, comparable scopes; this is a triage heuristic, not an SLA.

DBV8DBENG.meaning: Execution of a statement by the file database engine.
DBV8DBENG.read: Inspect Func, Sql and Context in the process serving the file infobase. duration is microseconds. Optional planSQLText uses file-engine operators such as FULL SCAN, USING INDEX and NESTED LOOP.
DBV8DBENG.badSigns: Repeated long file-engine operations; a FULL SCAN of a large source or nested scans are candidates when measured data volume explains the cost.
DBV8DBENG.traps: A scan operator alone does not prove a defect. File-engine plans have their own notation; SQL Server/PostgreSQL plan rules do not directly apply.
DBV8DBENG.fixes: Restrict the source data in the 1C query, inspect the file-engine plan and compare query/index alternatives over the whole operation.
DBV8DBENG.cost: Capturing every file-engine statement can be voluminous, especially with Sql, Context and plans.

TLOCK.meaning: Managed transactional lock acquisition; elapsed time includes acquisition waits, not the entire time the lock remains held.
TLOCK.read: Read Locks for resource values and modes, Regions for namespaces, and WaitConnections for conflicting t:connectID values. Find each participant's SDBL transaction boundaries; duration is microseconds.
TLOCK.badSigns: WaitConnections is non-empty, especially when unrelated business keys collide or cumulative acquisition time dominates posting.
TLOCK.traps: A short acquisition may hold a resource until a much later commit. Regions alone does not prove a whole-register lock; no WaitConnections is not evidence of a wait.
TLOCK.fixes: Capture all acquisitions and transaction boundaries; narrow lock dimensions, shorten transactions and use a consistent resource order after verifying intersections.
TLOCK.cost: All TLOCK acquisitions can be frequent; keep them during a short locks capture because a duration cutoff can remove the holder.

thresholds.text: The reference example collects managed-lock waits over 10 s using XML duration > 100000. This intentionally loses shorter acquisitions; the official lock methodology instead requires acquisitions without a duration cutoff to find holders.

TTIMEOUT.meaning: The maximum wait for a transactional lock was exceeded.
TTIMEOUT.read: Locate the victim with t:connectID, SessionID and Context; follow WaitConnections into TLOCK and SDBL on all participants. Obtain wait duration from the matching TLOCK, in microseconds.
TTIMEOUT.badSigns: A TTIMEOUT is already a failed lock wait; repeated instances in the same posting context indicate recurring contention.
TTIMEOUT.traps: TTIMEOUT can have zero duration. Its Context identifies the victim, not the transaction that originally acquired the resource.
TTIMEOUT.fixes: Use the locks profile to find the holder; shorten its transaction, reduce the protected resource scope and re-test concurrent posting.
TTIMEOUT.cost: Timeout records are incident-oriented; the acquisition and transaction evidence needed to explain them costs much more than this event alone.

TDEADLOCK.meaning: Detection of a deadlock in managed locking mode.
TDEADLOCK.read: Read DeadlockConnectionIntersections for participant pairs and intersecting resources. Recover their TLOCK acquisitions and SDBL transaction intervals, including short operations.
TDEADLOCK.badSigns: Any TDEADLOCK warrants cycle reconstruction; repeated participant contexts point to a reproducible access-order conflict.
TDEADLOCK.traps: Zero duration does not imply zero impact. This event does not represent every DBMS deadlock; DBMS cycles require the DBMS deadlock report.
TDEADLOCK.fixes: Align resource acquisition order and compatible lock modes in all participating BSL paths; repeat a parallel reproduction and check waits as well as deadlocks.
TDEADLOCK.cost: Deadlock incidents themselves are sparse; full unfiltered participant histories increase capture volume.

EXCP.meaning: Exception reported by the platform, application, network or DBMS; some exceptions accompany abnormal process termination.
EXCP.read: Preserve the entire Descr cause chain, Exception, OSException, Context and DumpFile when present. Use process/session and time to correlate PROC and EXCPCNTX.
EXCP.badSigns: A new recurring Descr, a failed user operation, or EXCP beside an abnormal PROC termination and dump.
EXCP.traps: Multiple components can log the same failure. Normalized Descr groups similar diagnostics but is not an incident count or a substitute for the full original.
EXCP.fixes: Fix the specific BSL/query/permission or environmental error identified by the cause chain; preserve exact platform version and dump for unexplained crashes.
EXCP.cost: Normally relatively small and infrequent according to the platform docs; repeated exceptions and long stacks can create an error storm.

EXCPCNTX.meaning: Snapshot of operations that had started but had not finished when an abnormal condition occurred.
EXCPCNTX.read: SrcName names the original event type. Read the emitted sequence from deepest nesting outward, together with EXCP, process identity and any dump.
EXCPCNTX.badSigns: Unfinished SQL or CALL frames accompanying a crash localize the interrupted operation; inspect the associated exception to classify failure.
EXCPCNTX.traps: These are interrupted-operation snapshots. [unverified] Counting them again as completed SQL/CALL work would distort throughput and duration totals.
EXCPCNTX.fixes: Investigate the deepest unfinished operation with the original exception; retain the stack and dump when escalating a platform failure.
EXCPCNTX.cost: Emission is tied to abnormal conditions rather than every successful call; a deep interrupted stack yields several records.

QERR.meaning: Query compilation or row/field access restriction error; also used for optional external-source NULL validation failures.
QERR.read: Read Descr, platform-language Query and Context under the failing user's permissions. Special NULL validation requires query checkActualNullable=true.
QERR.badSigns: The same Query fails repeatedly, only particular roles fail, or Descr reports a value inconsistent with external-source nullability.
QERR.traps: QERR diagnoses a query error, not a slow query. Enabling checkActualNullable can substantially slow query execution.
QERR.fixes: Correct query syntax or intended access rights; for external data reconcile nullable metadata and actual values rather than hiding the diagnostic.
QERR.cost: Ordinary QERR records follow failures; optional NULL checking adds execution overhead beyond the number of records written.

PROC.meaning: Lifecycle or availability event for an entire platform process, such as start, stop or abnormal termination.
PROC.read: Read process, PID and the lifecycle action/description; correlate the same process with EXCP, EXCPCNTX, ATTN and the configured restart policy.
PROC.badSigns: Explicit abnormal termination, or repeated unexplained worker replacement near failed operations.
PROC.traps: A normal stop/start can be scheduled recycling. Badanov's process-count examples depend on infrastructure and are not universal sizing limits.
PROC.fixes: For a crash preserve the dump and exact build; for excessive recycling compare cluster limits and OS resource measurements before changing settings.
PROC.cost: Platform docs classify PROC as relatively infrequent and small; retaining lifecycle history is cheaper than full SQL capture.

CONN.meaning: Establishment or loss of a client connection to the server.
CONN.read: Read the connection action, client/application, addresses and available identifiers; correlate the interval with SESN and process availability.
CONN.badSigns: Many clients reconnect beside EXCP or abnormal PROC records, rather than a single expected disconnect.
CONN.traps: Client connections, infobase sessions and DBMS connections are separate identities; this is not a log of every SQL connection.
CONN.fixes: Check the failing component and network path, then confirm process health and session restoration using the same reproduction.
CONN.cost: Usually low volume per the platform docs; a reconnection storm increases the number of CONN records.

SESN.meaning: Infobase session lifecycle and assignment of sessions to connections.
SESN.read: Use SessionID and Func with Usr and connection changes to follow the session across CONN events; inspect job history for scheduled work.
SESN.badSigns: [unverified] Repeated restoration or termination of the same workload beside CONN/EXCP is a diagnostic lead, not a standalone failure rule.
SESN.traps: A session can outlive a particular connection. SessionID can be absent when no session is assigned to the thread.
SESN.fixes: Investigate the associated connection loss or exception; compare scheduled-job execution history before changing job scheduling.
SESN.cost: SESN volume follows session creation, termination and reassignment; busy short-session workloads can emit many lifecycle records.

MEM.meaning: Growth in unfreed dynamic memory of a server process between checkpoints when no calls or scheduled jobs are running.
MEM.read: Compare sz/szd in bytes and cn/cnd as fragment counts for the same process. The event's duration spans the two eligible idle checkpoints, not a memory allocation call.
MEM.badSigns: Successive comparable runs leave positive szd/cnd and rising sz/cn; this is a lead for retained-object and dump analysis.
MEM.traps: Not periodic process RSS sampling. No eligible idle checkpoint or no mem generator can explain absent MEM even during memory growth.
MEM.fixes: Use LEAKS creation stacks to narrow retention; compare dumps of the same process before and after growth and inspect object lifetimes.
MEM.cost: The mem generator slows execution, especially parallel workloads; event volume follows observed checkpoint growth rather than a fixed sampling rate.

thresholds.text: The mem generator emits growth evidence between idle checkpoints when the number of allocated, unfreed fragments increases. There is no documented universal byte/MB leak threshold.

LEAKS.meaning: Objects retained between configured tracking checkpoints, with their types and creation stacks.
LEAKS.read: Read Descr for repeated object types and creation sites; relate surviving objects to the procedure or server-call checkpoint configured by leaks/point.
LEAKS.badSigns: Objects that are no longer needed accumulate after repeated completion of the same investigated procedure.
LEAKS.traps: A surviving object may still be required by application logic. Coverage is limited to tracked types and checkpoints, not every native allocation.
LEAKS.fixes: Narrow tracking to the implicated procedure; release unnecessary retained references and compare surviving objects after the same workload.
LEAKS.cost: Tracking object creation and checkpoints adds overhead; broad server-call checkpoints and creation stacks can be costly.

ATTN.meaning: Message from the cluster health-monitoring subsystem.

ATTN.badSigns: A process is reported unavailable or unresponsive, or memory has reached a configured critical limit.
ATTN.traps: A health warning reports a condition, not necessarily its initial cause; fields depend on the particular message and platform version.
ATTN.fixes: Check the affected process's exceptions and resource use; correct the demonstrated memory or availability constraint before adjusting cluster limits.
ATTN.cost: ATTN follows health notifications rather than every query; repeated critical-state messages can add sustained diagnostic volume.

SDGC.meaning: Cleanup and compaction of the session-data store.
SDGC.read: Follow InstanceID; compare FilesSize, UsedSize and CopyBytes in bytes by Method=Analyze/Compact. LockDuration is milliseconds, unlike record duration in microseconds.
SDGC.badSigns: UsedSize grows across comparable operations, or LockDuration spikes during the reported pause.
SDGC.traps: This is session-store maintenance, not collection of all BSL heap memory. Large FilesSize alone does not identify the code creating session data.
SDGC.fixes: Locate unnecessary session-data updates; temporarily use sessiondatacontext to obtain origins when needed, then reduce excessive changes.
SDGC.cost: Maintenance records are separate from MEM; sessiondatacontext adds diagnostic execution cost and should be temporary.

VRSREQUEST.meaning: Request to the server for a resource, exposing part of client/server interaction.
VRSREQUEST.read: Read URI, Method, Headers and Body, which is the body size in bytes. Use available vrs-session/sync identifiers to locate the matching response.
VRSREQUEST.badSigns: Many identical requests within one action, or request Body increasing with unnecessary form collections.
VRSREQUEST.traps: Starkov describes VRS correlation; uniform coverage across client modes is [unverified]. VRS intervals do not cover the complete user action.
VRSREQUEST.fixes: Combine unnecessary requests and defer form data that is not needed for opening; measure the action from before form creation.
VRSREQUEST.cost: Request frequency and recorded headers determine volume; all VRS traffic during interactive use can be numerous.

VRSRESPONSE.meaning: Server response to a resource request.
VRSRESPONSE.read: Inspect Status, Phrase, Headers and Body in bytes. Compare a correctly paired request/response interval with the application CALL interval.

SCRIPTCIRCREFS.meaning: Diagnostic report of circular references between BSL objects.
SCRIPTCIRCREFS.read: Inspect Context and reported object references to locate the assignments that retain the cycle; reproduce the implicated BSL procedure.

SCRIPTCIRCREFS.traps: Detection requires scriptcircrefs and can substantially slow the application; a cycle report does not quantify all process memory growth.
SCRIPTCIRCREFS.fixes: Remove the retaining reference cycle in the identified BSL objects, repeat the reproduction and disable detection afterward.

LIC.traps: Routine successful licensing actions are not faults. Property-name case varies in real JSON; software and hardware license paths differ.
LIC.fixes: Use the exact diagnostic to check available licenses, licensing configuration and hardware identity; verify the same launch can obtain a license.

ADDIN.meaning: External-component lifecycle and method execution, including failure of its host process.

ts.meaning: Completion timestamp in XML date-time notation, for example 2023-08-02T08:48:05.982000.

duration.meaning: Record elapsed duration in microseconds in JSON and modern text logs; 1000000 means one second.

durationus.meaning: XML duration-filter value in microseconds, not the JSON record's property name; 5000000 selects five seconds.
durationus.read: For manage_tech_log thresholdMs multiply milliseconds by 1000. Use zero/no cutoff when short calls or lock acquisitions must remain visible.
durationus.traps: Filtering on durationus reduces written events; it cannot reconstruct excluded short acquisitions or prove instrumentation is cheap.

Context.meaning: Execution context, generally a multiline BSL stack containing modules, lines and expressions.
Context.read: Follow the stack from the immediate operation back to callers; retain all frames when linking SQL to the BSL query or lock acquisition.
Context.traps: Missing or truncated Context cannot establish a complete caller path; inspect the original record. The context property must be captured.
nextSteps: search_in_code projectName=<project> query=<distinctive-frame-expression> fileMask=<metadata-folder>; then read_method_source projectName=<project> modulePath=<matched-path.bsl> methodName=<frame-method>.

Descr.meaning: Free-form diagnostic text; exceptions can contain a nested cause chain, while LEAKS includes retained-object descriptions and creation stacks.
Descr.read: For EXCP/QERR read the original cause chain before using a normalized group; for LEAKS compare object types and creation sites across checkpoints. ATTN Descr selects monitoring fields; SRVC encodes service[, infobase[, session]]: action; WINCERT names the failed Windows chain/policy API.
Descr.traps: One normalized exception description can group several occurrences or component reports; do not replace the original with the fingerprint.

Sql.meaning: Statement text in the physical database engine's SQL dialect, potentially including parameters and physical table names.
Sql.read: Use details to retain the exact SQL/parameters, locate its Context, and compare normalized count/total/max before inspecting a plan. Lowercase sql inside CLSTR Data is instead a reference-query timing in milliseconds, not statement text.
appearsIn: CLSTR Data subfield sql; a timing metric, not top-level SQL text
Sql.traps: Matching normalized SQL does not guarantee identical parameters, data volumes or execution plans.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=details path=<capture> groupId=<SQL-group-from-summary>; preserve parameters and Context before resolving the original BSL query.

Query.meaning: Query text associated with a platform query error, in the platform query language rather than physical DBMS SQL.
Query.read: Read beside QERR.Descr and Context to reproduce the error with the same roles and external-source metadata.
Query.traps: Do not send Query text directly to a DBMS as if it were Sql; permissions and platform compilation can fail before SQL execution.

planSQLText.meaning: Database-specific execution-plan text generated when plansql is enabled.
planSQLText.read: Locate expensive scan/join nodes and compare row estimates with measured rows where available. PostgreSQL actual time is milliseconds and rows/time must be interpreted with loops.
planSQLText.traps: Planner cost is not elapsed seconds. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement; the official PostgreSQL methodology limits plan capture to test/development.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=details path=<capture> groupId=<SQL-group>; preserve the complete plan and parameters, then resolve the Context frame with search_in_code projectName=<project> query=<frame-expression>.

Memory.meaning: Bytes allocated and not freed over a server call: a call-level memory change rather than process RSS.
Memory.read: Compare net retention for repeated equivalent CALL contexts; combine with MemoryPeak and same-process checkpoints/dumps to investigate growth.
Memory.traps: A positive net change can be legitimate retained state; this counter alone does not prove a leak.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=CALL property=Context contains=<module-or-method>; compare Memory with MemoryPeak across equivalent operations.

MemoryPeak.meaning: Peak bytes allocated but not freed during one server call.
MemoryPeak.read: Rank CALL occurrences by peak, then inspect their Context, returned data and report/form workload at comparable sizes.
MemoryPeak.traps: A high temporary peak can be released afterward; distinguish allocation pressure from persistent retention.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=details path=<capture> groupId=<memory-group-from-summary>; inspect the peak call occurrence and its Context before comparing the same workload.

CpuTime.meaning: CPU time consumed by CALL in microseconds; documented since platform 8.3.13.
CpuTime.read: Compare CPU and elapsed duration for the same call and its captured children to decide whether to profile computation or investigate waits. EVENTLOG uses CpuTime in microseconds for the indexed file portion, not a remote call.
CpuTime.traps: An absent CpuTime is unknown, not zero; do not sum resource counters across nested CALLs as independent work.
nextSteps: get_profiling_results responseFormat=detailed moduleFilter=<CALL-Context-module> after stop_profiling; EVENTLOG CpuTime instead needs event-log indexing inspection.

InBytes.meaning: Bytes read from disk during a server call, documented with CALL resource counters.
InBytes.read: Compare disk-read changes for the same CALL workload and inspect related queries and storage monitoring.
InBytes.traps: InBytes is disk input, even though some articles interpret it as client/server traffic. Use VRS Body for exchange size.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=chain path=<capture> occurrenceId=<CALL-occurrence>; examine DB work and disk I/O. For traffic, mode=describe property=Body.

OutBytes.meaning: Bytes written to disk during a server call.
OutBytes.read: Compare writes for equivalent posting/report operations and correlate with transaction and DB activity before examining storage behavior.
OutBytes.traps: OutBytes is not response-body or network byte count; nested call counters can overlap.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=CALL property=Context contains=<posting-method>; compare disk-write counters for equivalent operations.

Body.meaning: Size in bytes of the resource request or response body; the value is a size, not the payload text.
Body.read: Compare VRSREQUEST input and VRSRESPONSE output sizes per correctly paired interaction to find excessive form transfer.
Body.traps: CALL InBytes/OutBytes describe a different resource: disk I/O.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=VRSRESPONSE property=URI contains=<resource>; retain the method and request-side evidence before comparing response sizes.

process.meaning: Executable/component type such as rphost or 1cv8c, not a numeric PID.
process.read: Identify which component emitted an event before correlating its threads, lifecycle or server/client side of a call. The process metric nested inside CLSTR Data is instead a cluster-process endpoint.
appearsIn: all JSON event headers; availability of process/thread fields depends on producer
process.traps: Several processes can have the same process value; retain PID/source directory and time as well.

p:processName.meaning: Server infobase context, often the database name, stored as text.
p:processName.read: Use an exact value to narrow server events to the investigated infobase and verify capture scope before joining sessions.
p:processName.traps: Client or file-mode events may lack this property; an infobase filter can exclude those events.

OSThread.meaning: Operating-system thread identifier represented as a numeric string.
OSThread.read: Within one emitting process and interval, align nested event intervals/depth and identify candidate work on the same thread.
appearsIn: all JSON event headers; availability of process/thread fields depends on producer
OSThread.traps: [unverified] Equal thread numbers from different nodes/processes or distant time windows do not establish one execution chain.

SessionID.meaning: Infobase session identifier, not a platform or DBMS connection number.
SessionID.read: Follow SESN and CALL activity for the user's session, including changes of connection; narrow time and infobase before requesting chain.
SessionID.traps: May be absent when no session is assigned to a thread; the same session is not a unique call identifier.

t:connectID.meaning: Platform connection identifier used in transactional-lock participant correlation.
t:connectID.read: Follow a TLOCK/TTIMEOUT WaitConnections value to events carrying the matching t:connectID, then inspect their transaction boundaries.
t:connectID.traps: Do not equate its numeric value with SessionID, ClientID or dbpid.

ClientID.meaning: Remote-interaction client identifier, interpreted with the direction and destination of the call.
ClientID.read: Use SCALL ClientID/DstClientID and matching CALL identities with CallID and interface/method to identify candidate endpoints.
ClientID.traps: A numeric match alone does not prove a distributed call pair; node/process and temporal scope still matter.

CallID.meaning: Identifier of a remote call, represented as a numeric string.
CallID.read: Pair compatible SCALL/CALL records using client endpoints, method and interval, then inspect nested work on the receiving side.
CallID.traps: [unverified] Treat uniqueness over an entire multi-node archive as unproven; preserve endpoint and process scope.

dbpid.meaning: Identifier of the DBMS connection executing an operation.
dbpid.read: Map the 1C SQL event to DBMS wait/connection diagnostics; compare lksrc when finding a DBMS blocker.
dbpid.traps: This is a DBMS identity, not t:connectID; capture time and database are needed when investigating reused connections.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=<DBMS-event> property=dbpid contains=<connection-id>; contains is a substring filter, so verify the exact ID in each result.

Usr.meaning: Infobase user name, a textual attribution rather than a job identifier.
Usr.read: Compare failures under the affected user's roles and data; combine with session, application and job history for scheduled work.
Usr.traps: DefUser alone is not proof of a background job or its business outcome.

Func.meaning: Event-specific operation name, including data-model and lifecycle actions.
Func.read: For SDBL distinguish BeginTransaction, CommitTransaction, RollbackTransaction and HoldConnection from query work; for other events interpret Func in that event's semantics.
Func.traps: Do not count transaction or connection-management functions as executed SQL statements.

Rows.meaning: Number of rows returned by a database operation, recorded as a numeric value.
Rows.read: Compare returned volume to the user's needed result and CALL memory/transfer; inspect the plan separately for actual rows processed at each node.
Rows.traps: Rows is not scanned rows, pages read or an automatic measure of index efficiency.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=details path=<capture> groupId=<query-group>; compare the returned count with plan node rows/loops rather than inferring scanned rows.

RowsAffected.meaning: Affected-row count; Infostart's published event examples include the value -1.
RowsAffected.read: Compare known counts with the intended posting/exchange batch size and transaction/lock scope. Treat -1 as unknown for analysis until its meaning for that platform/operation is established.
RowsAffected.traps: Do not interpret -1 as a negative update count or replace it with zero.

Locks.meaning: Managed transactional lock resources, values and modes in the lock acquisition diagnostic.
Locks.read: Compare waiter and candidate holder resources for overlapping values and conflicting modes; inspect the BSL lock construction in Context.
Locks.traps: A namespace match alone does not establish the same protected keys or prove a whole-register lock.
nextSteps: manage_tech_log mode=preview profile=locks location=<new-absolute-directory>; include all short acquisitions when arranging a holder investigation.

Regions.meaning: Names of managed transactional lock namespaces.
Regions.read: Group contended business resources, then request Locks, Context and transaction intervals to establish their actual extent.
Regions.traps: Regions naming a register does not mean every record of that register was locked.

WaitConnections.meaning: List of platform connections conflicting over managed transactional locks.
WaitConnections.read: Non-empty values identify waiter-side leads: locate matching t:connectID acquisitions and their enclosing transactions across captured processes.
WaitConnections.traps: TLOCK without WaitConnections is not proof of waiting; a reported connection still needs resource/mode and lifetime checks.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=TLOCK property=WaitConnections contains=<holder-id>; then mode=chain occurrenceId=<waiter-occurrence> path=<same-capture>, checking exact IDs and resource scope.

DeadlockConnectionIntersections.meaning: Managed deadlock participant pairs and intersections of the locked resources.
DeadlockConnectionIntersections.read: Recover each listed participant's TLOCK acquisitions and transaction interval to reconstruct resource order in both BSL paths.
DeadlockConnectionIntersections.traps: A managed deadlock intersection is not a complete DBMS deadlock graph.

lka.meaning: DBMS blocking-source flag; value 1 means the thread was observed as a source by dbmslocks polling.
lka.read: Find the source's lkaid list, match a victim lkpid and inspect transaction history to locate the resource-acquiring operation.
lka.traps: Annotations attach to a later completed event; its SQL need not be the statement that acquired the lock.

lkp.meaning: DBMS blocking-victim flag; value 1 means the thread was observed waiting.
lkp.read: Read the same record's lkpid and lksrc, then find the source in other working-process logs.
lkp.traps: Observed blocking is not proof of a deadlock cycle; short waits can fall between polls.

lkpid.meaning: Identifier of the DBMS blocking poll attached to a victim, for example 423.
lkpid.read: Join this scalar value to an element of the source lkaid list across worker logs, then check lksrc and context.
lkpid.traps: lkpid is a poll identifier, not an OS PID, SQL statement id or platform connection id.

lkaid.meaning: Comma-separated list of blocking-poll identifiers on a source thread, for example 271,273,274.
lkaid.read: Split the list and find victim records with corresponding lkpid values; retain each participant's DBMS connection and transaction history.
lkaid.traps: The list is populated by dbmslocks observations, polled on DB access no more often than once per two seconds; it is not a continuous trace.

lksrc.meaning: DBMS connection identifier of the blocking source, present on the victim side.
lksrc.read: Use with the victim's lkpid and source's lkaid to identify the holder's dbpid and inspect its earlier transaction operations.
lksrc.traps: Do not resolve lksrc as a platform t:connectID or infer the holder solely from nearby timestamps.

lkpto.meaning: Seconds elapsed since the thread was detected as a DBMS blocking victim.
lkpto.read: Compare with poll linkage and surrounding event times to understand the observed wait history, then inspect the holder transaction.
lkpto.traps: Seconds since detection are neither record microseconds nor a precise timestamp of initial lock acquisition.

lkato.meaning: Seconds elapsed since the thread was detected as a DBMS blocking source.
lkato.read: Follow matching victims and the source's transaction completion to investigate how long the observed source state persists.
lkato.traps: Source-state age begins at detection; it is not the duration of the SQL carrying the annotation.

SrcName.meaning: Original operation's event type on an EXCPCNTX snapshot.
SrcName.read: Interpret each interrupted frame using the referenced event's semantics; read the EXCPCNTX sequence in descending nesting order.
SrcName.traps: SrcName=CALL describes an unfinished operation, not a second completed CALL.

LockDuration.meaning: Session-data store lock duration in milliseconds during garbage-collector work.
LockDuration.read: For a given SDGC InstanceID compare Analyze/Compact lock time with user pauses and changes in UsedSize/FilesSize.
LockDuration.traps: Do not divide this value by 1000 as if it were record duration in microseconds.

sz.meaning: Bytes of dynamic memory occupied by the process at a MEM checkpoint.
sz.read: Compare sz across equivalent idle checkpoints of the same process; combine with szd and retained-object evidence.
sz.traps: This is dynamic memory accounting at eligible checkpoints, not total OS RSS.

szd.meaning: Change in occupied dynamic-memory bytes since the previous MEM event.
szd.read: Follow repeated positive deltas after comparable completed operations and inspect LEAKS stacks or before/after dumps.
szd.traps: A single positive delta can be useful cached state; it does not establish erroneous retention.

cn.meaning: Count of occupied dynamic-memory fragments at a MEM checkpoint.
cn.read: Compare fragment-count growth with sz to distinguish more fragments from a few larger allocations in the same process.
cn.traps: Fragment count is not a count of BSL business objects or active sessions.

cnd.meaning: Change in occupied-fragment count since the previous MEM event.
cnd.read: Use alongside szd to identify repeated fragment accumulation and select comparable checkpoints for retention analysis.
cnd.traps: This delta has count units, not bytes; the interval depends on eligible idle checkpoints.

txt.meaning: Free-form diagnostic text; hardware-key records can encode operation(inputs)->outputs.
txt.read: Read the exact LIC action/result or HASP operation result; retain original spelling and casing when checking vendor documentation. CONN Txt contains ping-direction diagnostics; retain its event name and parameters.
txt.traps: Real samples use txt, Txt or TXT; property lookup must tolerate case variation without rewriting the original diagnostic.

Sdbl.meaning: Query text in the platform's database-model language, carried by SDBL.
Sdbl.read: Use the SDBL Context to find the BSL origin, then compare its nested physical Sql statements to see how the model operation was translated.
Sdbl.traps: Sdbl, QERR Query and DBMS Sql are different language layers, even when they describe the same business operation.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=SDBL property=Sdbl contains=<distinctive-query-fragment>; inspect the occurrenceId in mode=chain.

Action.meaning: Text description of configuration loading from files.
Action.read: Read the action text as a loading phase, not an outcome; correlate exceptions in the same load.

Admin.read: Text account name; use with ADMIN Func and time to attribute an administrative action.

agentURL.meaning: Address of the current server-agent process.
agentURL.read: Endpoint string; retain host and port when matching the working server.

All.meaning: Configuration selector enabling all event properties.
All.read: The property-filter selector all is configuration syntax, not a numeric counter in a record.

ApplicationExt.meaning: Refinement of a cluster functionality assignment requirement.
ApplicationExt.read: Text qualification; interpret with CLSTR Event and the applicable assignment rule.

AudioEncoding.read: Encoding name; compare the actual encoding to the selected recognition model.

AvMem.read: FTEXTUPD memory indicator; the supplied table does not state its unit, so do not assume bytes or compare it to MemoryPeak without build documentation.

BackgroundJobCreated.meaning: Whether full-text index construction ran in a background process.
BackgroundJobCreated.read: Boolean text true/false; this is execution placement, not successful completion.

BackupBaseFileName.meaning: Full-backup file used as the base of a differential binary-store backup.
BackupBaseFileName.read: Filesystem path; compare with BackupFileName and BackupType before identifying the backup chain.

BackupFileName.read: Filesystem path, not a database identifier; verify backup completion separately.

BackupType.read: Enumeration: 0 full, 1 differential; this value does not indicate operation success.

Calls.meaning: Number of client-to-server calls over TCP.
Calls.read: Call count; compare within the same operation and capture scope rather than treating it as elapsed time.

certificate.meaning: Identity of the certificate being checked by Windows.
certificate.read: Text includes subject, issuer and serial number sn; retain it with errorCode.

Class.meaning: Class in which an internal platform event was generated.
Class.read: Class name string; use with Component, File and Line for a support reproduction.

Classes.meaning: Objects exposed by an external component.
Classes.read: Pipe-separated object names; distinguish the class list from the one Type created or removed.

Cluster.meaning: Main port number of the server cluster.
Cluster.read: Numeric TCP port, not cluster UUID or worker PID; retain the host context.

Component.meaning: Platform component that generated an internal diagnostic.
Component.read: Component name text; keep the exact spelling for 1C support.

Connection.meaning: Infobase connection number, or the selected ICE candidate pair for video.
Connection.read: For VIDEOCONN this is local -> remote address text; elsewhere it is an infobase connection number. Never join those namespaces.

Connections.meaning: Connections for which the cluster lacked worker processes.
Connections.read: Connection count; interpret with the CLSTR Event, limits and available workers.

ConnLimit.meaning: Configured maximum connections per worker process.
ConnLimit.read: Count limit; compare it with the actual assignment event before changing capacity.

Contexts.meaning: Additional-grammar element count for speech recognition.
Contexts.read: Integer count of grammar elements; not a stack or a count of 1C sessions.

ContextsOnly.meaning: Whether speech recognition uses only the additional grammar.
ContextsOnly.read: Boolean flag text; compare to the requested grammar/model rather than HTTP context.

CopyBytes.meaning: Total size of values copied during session-store garbage collection.
CopyBytes.read: Bytes copied per SDGC operation; compare with UsedSize and LockDuration.

cpu.meaning: CPU load indicator in video connection diagnostics.
cpu.read: The property table names CPU load but does not specify scaling; retain raw units from the emitting build, not CpuTime microseconds. CLSTR Data explicitly reports cpu as percent; do not transfer that scaling to unspecified video metrics.

Crashed.meaning: Whether an external-component operation ended in error.
Crashed.read: Flag 1 marks error completion; use ErrorDescr and Result to identify the failed component action.

Database.meaning: Database location used by a database operation.
Database.read: Text server-name\database-name for client/server, full 1Cv8.1CD path for file mode; spelling/case variants such as DataBase resolve together.

DBConnID.meaning: Connection identity for an external data source.
DBConnID.read: Opaque source connection identifier; it is not the infobase t:connectID.

DBConnStr.meaning: Connection string for an external data source.
DBConnStr.read: Provider-specific text; inspect the target and options while protecting credentials in shared evidence.

DBCopy.meaning: Name of the database copy used by an operation.
DBCopy.read: Text copy name; absence means this property was not written for a copy access, not a freshness guarantee.

Dbms.meaning: Backend used by the operation that generated the event.
Dbms.read: Enumeration includes relational DBMS names, DBDA, file DBV8DBEng and EDS-only OLAP/MySQL/unknown backends; choose the matching dialect.

DBUsr.meaning: Database user of an external data source.
DBUsr.read: Source-account text, distinct from the infobase Usr; reproduce permission errors under this account.

description.meaning: Explanation of the data-history update action.
description.read: Free text; compare DHIST action and errors in that interval, not EXCP Descr normalization.

Direction.meaning: Direction of a media stream in video statistics.
Direction.read: Incoming/outgoing label; compare only the same direction and Type across samples.

DstAddr.meaning: Assigned worker-process address in cluster routing.
DstAddr.read: Endpoint string for the destination; compare with SrcAddr to see reassignment.

DstId.meaning: Unique identity of the assigned worker process.
DstId.read: Opaque unique process ID; distinct from numeric DstPid.

DstPid.meaning: OS process identifier of the assigned worker process.
DstPid.read: Integer PID; qualify by host and capture time before matching PROC records.

DstSrv.read: Host name text; compare with the preferred source server before blaming a remote route.

dumpError.meaning: Error that occurred while creating a process dump.
dumpError.read: Diagnostic text; a dump path alone does not establish that the dump was written successfully.

DumpFile.meaning: Name of the generated process-dump file.
DumpFile.read: Filesystem path; inspect dumpError and actual file availability when collecting crash evidence.

Err.read: Code 0 informational, 1 error; this is distinct from the event Level enumeration.

errorCode.meaning: Return code of the Windows certificate API operation.
errorCode.read: Preserve the original Windows error representation, commonly hexadecimal; decode for the specific verification API.

ErrorDescr.meaning: Exception text from an external-component operation.
ErrorDescr.read: Free-form ADDIN error text; compare MethodName and Result before grouping occurrences.

Event.meaning: Cluster action name which determines the other available properties.
Event.read: Text discriminant; current version older, routing and storage actions have different payloads.

Exception.read: Exception-type string; read the associated Descr cause chain before attributing the failure.

ExcessDurationSec.meaning: How long the cluster memory limit has been exceeded.
ExcessDurationSec.read: Seconds, not duration microseconds; inspect together with ExcessStartTime and configured MemoryLimits.

ExcessStartTime.meaning: Time when memory excess was detected.
ExcessStartTime.read: Recorded timestamp text; preserve the producer clock when relating the excess to workload.

ExtSrvcUrl.read: URL string; identify the exact receiver before comparing message-processing outcomes.

ExtSrvcUsr.meaning: Account used for the external integration service.
ExtSrvcUsr.read: User-name text at the integration endpoint; distinct from infobase session Usr.

FailedJobsCount.meaning: Full-text indexing background jobs that failed.
FailedJobsCount.read: Integer failure count; inspect their exceptions before interpreting update throughput.

File.meaning: Source file for SYSTEM, or index file with a full-text check problem.
File.read: File name/path text; meaning changes with event kind, so retain Component or FTEXTCHECK Info.

FileName.meaning: File holding the event-log index being built.
FileName.read: Filesystem name; pair with PacketCount and CpuTime for the same indexing operation.

Files.read: Text list of file names and sizes, present only with ftextupd logfiles=true; not a JSON array of paths.

FilesCount.meaning: Files in the directory used by a full-text update.
FilesCount.read: Integer count, emitted only with extended logfiles diagnostics; absence is unknown rather than zero files.

FilesSize.meaning: Total size of the session-data store.
FilesSize.read: Bytes; compare to UsedSize for the same InstanceID across SDGC operations.

FilesTotalSize.meaning: Size of files in the full-text update directory.
FilesTotalSize.read: Size indicator emitted with ftextupd logfiles=true; the table does not specify a unit, so confirm the build before converting it.

FillRefsPresent.meaning: Use of the value-list reference cache for input-by-string.
FillRefsPresent.read: Presence marker, not a full-text result count; a present marker means cache references were used.

FindByString.read: Configuration object name text; use with Text and timing to reproduce the lookup.

findTicks.meaning: Time spent searching the database during input-by-string.
findTicks.read: Milliseconds; compare with ftextTicks and fallback flags for the same entered text.

Finish.read: Reason text; check whether it explicitly indicates abnormal termination before diagnosing a crash.

fixedState.meaning: New indexed-through point in the full-text state file.
fixedState.read: ISO 8601 timestamp; compare successive values within the same index/job context.

Folder.meaning: Directory acted on during full-text indexing.
Folder.read: Path to index or temporary directory, available with logfiles=true; not necessarily the permanent index directory.

Frames.meaning: Audio frames in a speech-recognition stream.
Frames.read: Integer frame count; not seconds without the actual stream format and frame duration.

FreeMemory.meaning: Free RAM on the computer hosting the server cluster.
FreeMemory.read: Memory-volume value; the property table does not state scaling, so verify emitting-build units before comparing external OS counters.

ftextResultCount.meaning: References found by full-text search for input-by-string.
ftextResultCount.read: Integer count; compare with tooManyResults before assuming all references were used.

ftextSearchCount.read: Integer call count for the lookup; compare with entered text and fallback behavior.

ftextTicks.meaning: Time spent in full-text search during input-by-string.
ftextTicks.read: Milliseconds; subtracting it from record duration requires converting microseconds first and checking interval overlap.

fullKey.meaning: Complete key used to find a record in the search engine.
fullKey.read: Opaque key text; preserve the exact value when locating the failed FTS record.

Headers.meaning: HTTP headers of a resource request or response.
Headers.read: Header text, potentially multiline; retain request/response direction and redact authorization/cookies in shared examples.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=VRSRESPONSE property=URI contains=<resource>; inspect original Headers and Status for the affected interaction.

Host.meaning: Computer name associated with the recorded operation.
Host.read: Host-name string; qualify process and connection IDs by host when combining logs.

IB.read: Database-name text; combine with server identity to distinguish equal names on different hosts.

IBLimit.meaning: Maximum infobases assigned to a worker process.
IBLimit.read: Configured count limit; interpret the CLSTR capacity event rather than treating it as current usage.

Id.meaning: Binary-store object identity, or streaming speech-session identity.
Id.read: Opaque object/session identifier; qualify by STORE versus STT/STTADM before correlating.

IName.meaning: Interface name for a remote invocation.
IName.read: Text interface name; use Interface, Method and MName to distinguish methods sharing a display name.

Info.meaning: Full-text check fault information, or failed process-connection attempts in cluster monitoring.
Info.read: FTEXTCHECK uses diagnostic text; ATTN uses an attempt count. Read according to the event, not a shared numeric decoder.

Infobases.meaning: Infobases for which the cluster lacked worker processes.
Infobases.read: Integer count; correlate CLSTR routing and limits to establish the capacity shortage.

InMessage.meaning: Control messages received from the thin client by the video module.
InMessage.read: Message text; follow VIDEOCALL sequence rather than treating it as incoming media bytes.

InstanceID.read: Integer identifier; compare SDGC sizes only within the same store and producer scope.

JobCanceledByLoadLimit.meaning: Whether a full-text indexing job was cancelled because the worker reached its load limit.
JobCanceledByLoadLimit.read: Boolean flag text; distinguish capacity cancellation from FailedJobsCount errors.

jobId.read: Opaque job identity; use it to restrict FTS events, not as a platform SessionID.

Key.read: Opaque speech-session key; correlate selected model and stream properties within that key.

Level.read: Enumeration TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARNING or ERROR; this is severity, not stack depth.

Line.meaning: Source line that generated an internal diagnostic.
Line.read: Integer source line; interpret with SYSTEM File and Class rather than a BSL Context module.

Location.read: Path or object-identifier text depending on ADDIN Func; inspect Type/MethodName before interpreting.

logFrom.meaning: Start timestamp of an event-log portion processed by full-text indexing.
logFrom.read: ISO 8601 timestamp; compare logTo in the same portion rather than the event completion ts.

logTo.meaning: End timestamp of an event-log portion processed by full-text indexing.
logTo.read: ISO 8601 timestamp; follow successive portions to check progress independently of wall-clock job duration.

MDX.meaning: Query sent to an OLAP external data source.
MDX.read: MDX text, not relational SQL; inspect the corresponding EDS backend and source query tooling.

MemoryLimits.meaning: Configured memory limits reported by cluster monitoring.
MemoryLimits.read: Structured limit text; distinguish the configured temporary/critical limits from measured process allocation.

MemoryUsed.meaning: Maximum dynamic memory used during full-text indexing work.
MemoryUsed.read: Memory-volume indicator; units are unspecified in this property table, so preserve the reported value until build units are verified.

Message.meaning: Message passed by an external-component event.
Message.read: Application-supplied text; compare Source and Func before treating it as a platform exception.

MessageUid.meaning: Identity of the mail message that failed parsing.
MessageUid.read: InternetMailMessage identifier string; retain it with Method to reproduce the failing message operation.

metaDataId.meaning: Unique metadata object identity of an indexed table.
metaDataId.read: UUID-like metadata identifier; resolve it in the XML export of the investigated configuration.

Method.read: CALL/SCALL uses an interface method number; VRS uses an HTTP verb; mail uses GET/GETHEADERS/SETRAW; SDGC uses Compact/Analyze. Preserve the event discriminator.

MethodName.read: Method-name text; inspect ADDIN Result/ErrorDescr for this exact method.

MinDataId.meaning: Minimum data ID in the indexing portion exchanged with a worker.
MinDataId.read: Identifier, not a record count; compare full-text update portions before inferring progress.

MinimalWriteSize.meaning: Size above which values are written to the binary-data store.
MinimalWriteSize.read: Configured size threshold; the supplied table does not state units, so verify the build before changing it.

MName.read: Method-name string; match with IName, CallID and endpoint identities when pairing CALL/SCALL.

modelID.read: Opaque model identifier; compare requested tx:* and selected rx:* version/language for the same model.

MyVer.meaning: Current server-state version in a cluster action.
MyVer.read: Version token; compare SrcVer for current version older rather than treating it as the platform release.

Name.meaning: Event name in the technological-log record.
Name.read: Case-insensitive event-name text; JSON writes name, distinct from Func and Level.

NeedResync.meaning: Whether cluster service data must be synchronized.
NeedResync.read: Flag on CLSTR Event=current version older; interpret with MyVer/SrcVer, not as a database-copy lag duration.

NewServiceDataDirectory.meaning: Service data directory after a settings change and cluster restart.
NewServiceDataDirectory.read: Filesystem path; compare OldServiceDataDirectory and the service identity in the same CLSTR event.

Nmb.meaning: Session number in a session-lifecycle event.
Nmb.read: Numeric session identity; do not equate it to the infobase connection number.

NParams.meaning: File-database SQL parameters used to transfer long binary data.
NParams.read: Integer parameter count; not the number of returned rows or the complete SQL parameter text.

Obsolete.meaning: Old worker processes reported by the cluster.
Obsolete.read: Count and unique identifiers in text; inspect the CLSTR transition before treating obsolete workers as crashed.

OldServiceDataDirectory.meaning: Service data directory before a settings change.
OldServiceDataDirectory.read: Filesystem path; retain it with NewServiceDataDirectory for the affected service, not a global infobase path.

OSException.read: Native exception text; compare with platform Exception and dump evidence before assigning root cause.

OutMessage.meaning: Video control messages sent to the thin client.
OutMessage.read: Message text, not outgoing video-stream size; compare corresponding VIDEOCALL control transitions.

PacketCount.meaning: Packets actually written to the event-log index for the current file.
PacketCount.read: Integer packet count; compare FileName and CpuTime, not DB Rows.

parallelism.meaning: Allowed parallel background jobs for full-text indexing.
parallelism.read: Configured concurrent-job count; raising it affects CPU and memory demand and is not proof of queue starvation.

Path.read: Filesystem path; use with modelID and Type to locate a failed model component.

Phrase.meaning: HTTP status phrase, or a speech additional-grammar element count.
Phrase.read: VRSRESPONSE uses text such as OK; STT/STTADM uses an element count. Do not interpret speech Phrase as transcription text.

PID.read: Integer PID; ATTN identifies the main cluster manager. Combine with host and time to handle PID reuse.

Port.meaning: Main network port of the process.
Port.read: Numeric TCP port; this differs from SyncPort and the cluster main-port field Cluster.

ProcessId.meaning: Unique cluster-process identity in monitoring diagnostics; inspect Descr to distinguish the main manager from another cluster process.
ProcessId.read: Opaque process identifier, distinct from numeric OS PID; the detailed ATTN Descr variants can refer to a manager or worker process.

ProcessName.meaning: Name of the process or server shared-data context.
ProcessName.read: Text name; SCOM shared-data lifetimes may pair it with srcProcessName, so do not assume an executable path.

procURL.meaning: Address of the server process to which the event belongs.
procURL.read: Endpoint string; retain host and port when correlating worker incidents.

QueryFileds.meaning: Query fields with unexpected NULL values.
QueryFileds.read: Field-name list text; preserve the documented spelling QueryFileds and inspect QERR Query and external-source metadata.

QueueLenght.meaning: CPU request-queue length in video connection diagnostics.
QueueLenght.read: Integer queue count; the reference spells it QueueLenght. It is not a background-job scheduler queue.

ReadOnlyMode.meaning: Whether the binary-data store is read-only.
ReadOnlyMode.read: Boolean flag text; compare a failed STORE write with the configured mode.

Reason.meaning: Reason a worker process was unavailable.
Reason.read: Diagnostic text belonging to CLSTR Event; check routing/capacity context before assigning an OS failure.

recordCount.meaning: Records before or after indexing in a full-text portion.
recordCount.read: Integer count; distinguish this portion from cumulative totalRecords.

Recording.meaning: Whether the recognition audio stream is recorded.
Recording.read: Boolean recording flag; this does not indicate successful recognition or the recording duration.

recordRef.meaning: Internal reference to an indexed table record.
recordRef.read: Opaque reference string; use with tableName/metaDataId to locate the specific FTS error.

Ref.meaning: Infobase name associated with an operation.
Ref.read: Text name; it is not a metadata object reference and needs server scope for cross-node comparison.

Registered.meaning: New worker processes reported by the cluster.
Registered.read: Count and unique identifiers in text; distinguish registration from readiness or successful workload execution.

reindexCount.read: Integer table count; repeated reindexing requires error/progress evidence before diagnosing an update storm.

Released.meaning: Reserve workers that became primary workers.
Released.read: Count and unique identifiers in text; interpret the CLSTR lifecycle change, not memory release.

Report.meaning: Metadata name of a report running as a background job.
Report.read: Report-name string; locate its module and job history instead of using Usr alone to identify the job.

Request.read: Opaque request ID; match routing actions within the cluster, not HTTP request bodies.

res.meaning: Action of the platform licensing system.
res.read: LIC action text such as seize or reuse; inspect txt for attempted hardware/software licence sources and failure reasons.

Result.meaning: Event-specific result of an index check or external-component operation.
Result.read: FTEXTCHECK: 1 no errors, 0 errors. ADDIN: 0 success, 1 failure. The code has no universal interpretation across events.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=FTEXTCHECK property=Result contains=0 to inspect failed checks; for ADDIN, failure uses Result=1 instead.

thresholds.text: Use event-specific codes: FTEXTCHECK 1=no errors, 0=errors; ADDIN 0=success, 1=failure.

RetExcp.meaning: Server-call exception returned to the client as the call result.
RetExcp.read: Exception text on CALL; inspect the related EXCP cause chain and receiver Context rather than assuming normal return.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=CALL property=RetExcp contains=<exception-fragment>; then inspect its occurrenceId in mode=chain.

RunAs.read: Enumeration application or service; use the service account's configuration directory when checking capture pickup.

SafeLimit.meaning: Safe memory expenditure per call in cluster monitoring.
SafeLimit.read: Memory-limit value; units are not stated in the supplied property table. Compare against FreeMemory only after confirming build units.

seanceID.read: Session identity string; do not silently equate it with a TCP client or DBMS connection identifier.

SearchByMask.meaning: Database search without using full-text results for input-by-string.
SearchByMask.read: Flag TRUE or 1 means database search is used; inspect tooManyResults and Text to understand fallback.

Separation.meaning: Whether data separation is enabled for a full-text check.
Separation.read: Boolean-like separation flag; interpret SepId only in the corresponding separation scope.

SepId.meaning: Separation-area index for a full-text index check.
SepId.read: Area index value; a repeated file name in another area is not necessarily the same index instance.

ServerComputerName.read: Host-name text; scope PIDs and resource incidents to this server.

ServerId.meaning: Unique server identity in cluster monitoring.
ServerId.read: Opaque server ID; distinguish it from ProcessId and PID in the same ATTN diagnostic.

ServiceName.meaning: Name of the cluster service involved in an action.
ServiceName.read: Service-name string; interpret with CLSTR Event to identify the affected service transition.

Size.meaning: Size of an object written to the cluster binary store.
Size.read: Object-size value; table units are unspecified, so verify emitting-build units before converting it to bytes.

skippedRecords.meaning: Records skipped because of full-text indexing errors.
skippedRecords.read: Integer count; retrieve the associated failed record/job details instead of treating skips as successful indexing.

Source.meaning: Source supplied when an external component raises an event.
Source.read: Application-defined source string; compare Message and the component Type, not OS source files.

SrcAddr.meaning: Preferred worker-process address before cluster assignment.
SrcAddr.read: Endpoint string; compare assigned DstAddr to establish which worker was actually chosen.

SrcId.meaning: Unique identity of the preferred worker process.
SrcId.read: Opaque unique process identifier; distinguish it from numeric SrcPid and assigned DstId.

SrcPid.meaning: OS PID of the preferred worker process.
SrcPid.read: Integer process number; correlate with host/time before examining process lifecycle.

srcProcessName.meaning: Original shared-infobase-data name at creation, recorded when releasing it.
srcProcessName.read: Text name; compare current ProcessName to trace the same SCOM shared-data lifetime.

SrcURL.read: Server endpoint string; differs from preferred process SrcAddr and destination DstAddr.

SrcVer.read: Version token; compare to MyVer for synchronization events rather than platform binary versions.

SrvcName.read: Configuration metadata name; resolve this service before inspecting its ExtSrvcUrl endpoint.

State.meaning: Start or completion state of a full-text update operation.
State.read: State marker text; match the update phase and job before claiming successful index completion.

Status.meaning: HTTP response code, speech-component result, or video-connection state.
Status.read: VRSRESPONSE uses an HTTP numeric code; STT/STTADM uses model-component status; VIDEOCONN uses connection state. Interpret by event kind.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=VRSRESPONSE property=Status contains=<code>; this substring filter needs exact-code verification and does not apply to speech/video status semantics.

StorageGUID.read: GUID string; compare STORE operations only within that store, not SDGC InstanceID.

StreamType.meaning: Client media stream used by a video connection.
StreamType.read: Enumeration video, audio or screen; separate streams before interpreting connection transitions.

SyncPort.meaning: Auxiliary network port of a process.
SyncPort.read: Numeric port; it is distinct from the primary Port when diagnosing endpoint accessibility.

t:applicationName.meaning: Client-program identity assigned to the current thread.
t:applicationName.read: Application-name string; use with session and actual job history to distinguish scheduler work.

t:clientID.read: Opaque client connection ID; not the infobase t:connectID or DBMS Dbpid.

t:computerName.meaning: Client computer name associated with the thread.
t:computerName.read: Host-name string; retain producer versus client-host distinction in cross-node analysis.

tableCode.meaning: Full-text table code when the table name is unavailable.
tableCode.read: Opaque code; absence of tableName does not mean no table was indexed.

tableCount.meaning: Tables before or after indexing in a full-text portion.
tableCount.read: Integer count for the portion; compare recordCount separately to estimate actual data work.

tableName.meaning: Table involved in a full-text indexing operation.
tableName.read: Table-name text; resolve with metaDataId/tableRef in the same configuration version.

tableRef.meaning: Human-readable reference to the configuration object being indexed.
tableRef.read: Metadata-reference text; use it to locate the affected object in the EDT project.

Text.read: User-entered text; reproduce the exact search pattern while anonymizing shared examples.

Time.meaning: Full-text update output time, or FTS operation time.
Time.read: FTEXTUPD uses output time; FTS uses milliseconds or ddd.hh:mm:ss.fff interval text. Do not parse both as a timestamp.

tooManyResults.meaning: Too many matching full-text references, forcing input-by-string fallback.
tooManyResults.read: Flag TRUE or 1 means full-text results are not used; inspect ftextResultCount and database findTicks.

TotalJobsCount.meaning: Background processes created during full-text indexing.
TotalJobsCount.read: Integer created-job count; not the number concurrently running or waiting in a scheduler queue.

TotalMemory.meaning: RAM volume of the computer hosting the server cluster.
TotalMemory.read: Memory-volume indicator; confirm emitting-build units before comparing to process counters or an external RAM limit.

totalRecords.meaning: Cumulative records in a full-text indexing portion.
totalRecords.read: Integer accumulated count; compare within the same portion/job to avoid summing repeated cumulative values.

Trans.meaning: Whether a transaction was already active when the event began.
Trans.read: Flag 0 no open transaction, 1 open transaction; it is not a transaction ID or a transaction duration.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=SDBL property=Func contains=Transaction; inspect begin/commit/rollback markers for the same infobase connection.

Type.meaning: External-component object type, speech-model component kind, or video media type.
Type.read: ADDIN uses a type name; speech uses acoustics/grammar; VIDEOSTATS uses video/audio. Retain the event discriminator.

URI.read: URI text on VRS request/response; compare the same method/resource and preserve correlation before measuring response sizes.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=VRSREQUEST property=URI contains=<resource>; compare matching response evidence without assuming adjacency proves pairing.

Url.meaning: Address of the main cluster manager in monitoring diagnostics.
Url.read: Endpoint string; use it to identify the manager rather than the external integration-service URL.

UsedSize.meaning: Used space inside the session-data store.
UsedSize.read: Bytes; compare to FilesSize for the same SDGC InstanceID to distinguish useful data growth from unused store space.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=SDGC property=InstanceID contains=<store-id>; compare exact-store UsedSize/FilesSize and LockDuration over time.

UseMode.meaning: Whether cluster binary-data storage is used.
UseMode.read: Usage flag; inspect the actual STORE operation and ReadOnlyMode before interpreting a write failure.

Val.meaning: Value whose meaning is selected by Func.
Val.read: Operation-dependent text; resolve the specific Func before assigning a unit or treating it as a size/count.

Value.meaning: Media-stream statistics in video connection diagnostics.
Value.read: Statistics text; preserve named metrics and their reported units instead of using one scalar decoder.

Word.meaning: Word identified during full-text index validation.
Word.read: Text, present when a word is identified; inspect File and Info to reproduce the precise check failure.

Meth.read: Meth is a procedure/function name in CALL diagnostics; resolve the named Module before using read_method_source.

Data.meaning: Cluster performance-update metrics encoded as parameter=value pairs.
Data.read: Comma-separated text on CLSTR Event=performance update; cpu is percent, timing metrics are milliseconds, and process is an endpoint here rather than the top-level executable name.

Deficit.meaning: Worker processes missing when the cluster detects a process shortage.
Deficit.read: Integer worker count on CLSTR Event=process deficit detected; compare Connections and Infobases before inferring a background-job queue.

ByMemory.meaning: Worker identities selected for restart because of memory usage.
ByMemory.read: Process-identifier list text on CLSTR Event=process restart required; not a byte counter or evidence that every listed worker has already stopped.

ByTime.meaning: Worker identities selected for restart because of lifetime.
ByTime.read: Process-identifier list text on the restart-required CLSTR action; distinguish lifetime policy from a memory-induced restart.

average_response_time.read: Milliseconds averaged over the documented five-minute interval inside CLSTR Data; not mean business-request latency.

disk_performance.read: Milliseconds inside CLSTR Data; compare the same worker and reference workload, not query duration.
nextSteps: get_tech_log mode=events path=<capture> event=CLSTR property=Event contains=performance; inspect the metric inside Data rather than filtering a nonexistent top-level metric key.

errors.meaning: Diagnose reported failures and loss of component availability without collecting every successful call or SQL statement.
errors.read: Use for an exception, failed query, disconnect or crash. Read EXCP/QERR first, correlate PROC/CONN/SESN/ATTN, and treat TTIMEOUT/TDEADLOCK as leads requiring participant history; the cutoff is 0 ms.
errors.traps: It does not collect all TLOCK acquisitions or SDBL transaction boundaries, so it cannot identify every holder from an incident alone. Dump generation is separate.
errors.fixes: Repair the exact diagnostic's cause; switch to locks when timeout/deadlock participants are missing.
errors.cost: Normally smaller than SQL capture per platform docs; long exception chains and error/reconnection storms can still be large.

slow-calls.meaning: Find receiving server contexts and outgoing calls that exceed the chosen individual-call cutoff.
slow-calls.read: Use after a slow operation is localized. The default 1000 ms cutoff selects CALL/SCALL; compare count, total/max duration, Context, CpuTime and MemoryPeak, then inspect EXCP for failure.
slow-calls.traps: Short repeated calls are excluded by the default cutoff; nested CALL/SCALL durations overlap, so their totals are not full-user-operation time.
slow-calls.fixes: Use scenario to identify whether SQL, lock waits, computation or form exchange dominates the expensive context, then optimize that component.
slow-calls.cost: Volume falls as the cutoff rises; frequent long calls with full stacks can remain numerous, and filtering hides accumulated short-call cost.

db.meaning: Locate expensive physical SQL and platform data-model operations before a focused plan investigation.
db.read: Use when database work dominates. The default 5000 ms cutoff applies to physical DB events; SDBL and EXCP/QERR remain unfiltered. Inspect Sql/Sdbl, Context and count/total/max. Plans and DBMS lock polling are explicit options.
db.traps: The five-second cutoff is a diagnostic choice, not a platform health limit. Gilev's historical example uses ten seconds; IBS uses five. Official PostgreSQL guidance confines plans to test/development, unlike older article profiles.
db.fixes: Find the BSL query and inspect data, parameters, statistics and waits before changing predicates or indexes; lower the cutoff for repeated short SQL.
db.cost: IBS reports hundreds of MB even above five seconds. SQL/parameters enlarge records; optional plans/polling add overhead beyond output volume.

locks.meaning: Reconstruct managed lock waits, transaction lifetimes and optional observed DBMS blocker relationships.
locks.read: Use during a short concurrent reproduction on all relevant workers. The 0 ms cutoff keeps TLOCK acquisitions, TTIMEOUT/TDEADLOCK, SDBL boundaries and server SQL; optional dbmslocks adds lka/lkp poll linkage.
locks.traps: Filtering short acquisitions loses holders. The bundled event set includes SQL Server, PostgreSQL and file-engine (DBV8DBENG) SQL. Poll linkage does not prove a DBMS deadlock cycle.
locks.fixes: Check WaitConnections, resource values/modes and transaction lifetime; then shorten scope or align resource order. Obtain a DBMS deadlock report for DBMS cycles.
locks.cost: High acquisition and SQL frequency can produce a large log; bound the reproduction and retain logs from every participant, including short successful holders.

memory.meaning: Separate high call allocation peaks from persistent object retention in one server process.
memory.read: Use after reproducible memory growth. CALL counters localize peaks; mem enables MEM idle-checkpoint counters, and leaks collect=1 with point call=server enables retained-object stacks. The cutoff is 0 ms.
memory.traps: MEM is not periodic RSS; no suitable idle checkpoint can explain absence. LEAKS tracks selected objects and surviving objects can be legitimate; compare the same process/workload.
memory.fixes: Narrow retained-object tracking to the implicated procedure after localization and compare same-process before/after dumps; reduce unnecessary collections or retained references.
memory.cost: mem/leaks instrumentation slows execution, especially parallel workloads; broad checkpoints and creation stacks are more costly than CALL counters alone.

scenario.meaning: Explain one complete reproduced user action across calls, data access, locks and resource exchanges.
scenario.read: Start immediately before one short reproduction and stop immediately after it. At 0 ms, retain CALL/SCALL, VRS request/response, SDBL, database events, managed locks and errors; find the enclosing call and compare child intervals.
scenario.traps: A server-only capture can miss client transfer/reconstruction and other nodes. historyHours=1 is retention, not automatic capture expiry; an unfinished call may not yet have a completion record.
scenario.fixes: Follow details then chain, test the demonstrated query/lock/call/form correction and repeat with the same data, timing boundary and concurrency.
scenario.cost: Potentially the largest bundled profile because it retains short calls and SQL; stop explicitly after the reproduction rather than leaving it as permanent monitoring.

exceptions.meaning: A platform, application or infrastructure exception interrupted or threatened the operation.
exceptions.evidence: EXCP Exception/Descr and Context establish the reported failure; the complete cause chain and user outcome establish impact. Several matching component records do not establish several independent incidents.
